newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania PM defends reform record.
newsitem.headline: Romania PM defends reform record.

text.p: Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea defended his shock-therapy for the Romanian economy on Tuesday, insisting that "the way we've chosen is right".

Summing up almost six months since his centrist government took office, Ciorbea told reporters that liberalisation of prices, cuts in state subsidies and the central bank's tough monetary policy prove the cabinet's commitment to reform.
Prices have risen sharply under the IMF-backed reform programme and a series of loss-making companies have been slated for closure but the government has so far been spared major labour unrest.

Ciorbea said the central bank's foreign exchange reserves had risen to $1.6 billion, more than double the level in February, which he said was vital for economic recovery and to keep the monetary policy under control.
"On June 3, the government will assume in front of parliament its responsibility for the programme which includes the whole package of economic reforms," he said.
